newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan says Mideast conference "golden opportunity".
newsitem.headline: Jordan says Mideast conference "golden opportunity".

text.p: Jordan's Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawnah was quoted on Saturday as saying his country would attend this year's Middle East economic conference between Israel and its Arab neighbours.
Tarawnah told Ad-Dustour newspaper the conference was a "golden opportunity" for business in the region and said Arab states could use it to overcome differences with Israel.
"We have a clear position...to attend the conference if it is held," the paper quoted Tarawnah as saying.

Saudi Arabia has already said it would not attend the conference in November. Other key Arab states, including Egypt and Morocco, have decided to wait for progress in peace talks between Israel and the Palestinians before deciding.
"If there are differences with Israel, why should we let slip the golden opportunity of this conference," Tarawnah said.

Israeli-PLO talks collapsed in March after Israel enraged Palestinians by starting work on a new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem. Palestinians and Israeli troops have had running clashes in the West Bank town of Hebron for a week.
The annual conferences, launched in Casablanca in 1994, are meant to promote peace in the Middle East through trade and economic cooperation between Israel and its Arab neighbours.

Jordan hosted the 1995 conference followed in 1996 by Egypt, which came close to cancelling the Cairo meeting for fear that the recently elected right-wing government in Israel would scare away many of the potential participants.
Tarawnah, responding to Arab fears that Israel was using the conferences as a platform to dominate the Middle East economy, said no one was forcing Arabs to do business with the Jewish state.
"We do not believe that Israel will determine the movement in the region," he said.
Tarawnah likened stalled Israeli-Palestinian talks to a business cycle.

"There are ups and downs, and we believe we are now at a low because the process has reached a negotiating crisis... but I still feel there is an Arab and international readiness to rescue the situation," he said.
